coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Slaughter is regulated by Decreto 59/1993 on fresh meat and a 1996 decree. The Dipartimento Sanità keeps a list of approved slaughterhouses, and an official veterinarian inspects and stamps each carcass (ISS pages documento49000615/49000625, faolex smr51589). The competent authority for food hygiene is ISS Dipartimento Prevenzione, UOS Sanità Veterinaria e Igiene Alimentare. The hygiene regulation excludes retail shops from the HACCP-plan duty (ISS documento49000665, art. 5), and the meat decree exempts cutting and storage in retail shops. So butchers carry little recurring paperwork beyond the licence. The licensing circular OSLA 6/2020 may require an ISS authorisation or self-certification for some licences; unverified for butchers. Operators must register with the Servizio Igiene Ambientale when receiving goods from another State, except retail licence-holders of animal products (old decree, faolex smr47771, still in force unverified). Nothing new beyond K07 (food producers). A few abattoirs and butchers are not enough for a product.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: UPAV (Ufficio Prevenzione Ambiente e Vigilanza del Territorio) authorises abstraction of surface and groundwater. Its leaflet (rev. 15/04/2024, gov.sm, non-binding) covers domestic use only, excluding drinking: cleaning, gardening, agriculture. A well is a building work needing an approved project. Abstraction needs form A14 plus a cadastral plan, a declaration of method and frequency, and a report by a geologist or engineer. Fee is EUR 70 on paper and EUR 60 electronic. Surface-water authorisations may need annual renewal. Summer restriction orders can suspend abstraction. A census of wells and cisterns was requested by a council motion; whether it was carried out is unknown. Legal base: DD 44/2012 (Environmental Code, art. 93 water management plan) and Regolamento 1/2019. Households and farms file occasionally, so volume is tiny; see candidate C1.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Public water is run by AASS and monitored by the ISS public-health laboratory (650+ samples a year, 67 parameters, results published every 6 months under EU Directive 2020/2184 principles). No private small-system operator duties were found. The weak point cited in a council document is the household plumbing. Mostly state-run, so not a market. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Street trading ('commercio ambulante': retail or wholesale using mobile equipment only) is covered by DD 18/12/2023 n.185 'Disciplina delle attività economiche', ratified as DD 14/03/2024 n.50. Earlier laws were Legge 111/1982 and Legge 130/2010. DD 103/2016 covers food and drink sales on public areas. Licence holders must be actual, continuous residents. The articles on pitches and markets were not reached. No San Marino market-operator or pitch-allocation software need was found. Money changers: no source found on who licenses them; they are likely banks or intermediaries under BCSM, with AML duties under Law 92/2008 (amended by DD 116/2017); unverified. Nothing strong.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Confirmed: pharmacies are ISS-run (UOC Farmaceutica, seven pharmacies reorganised in 2019 by Congresso di Stato delibera 20/2019; Cailungo, Città di San Marino, Borgo Maggiore, Serravalle, Gualdicciolo). No private pharmacy was found in any result, so the buyer is the state and it is out of scope. Narcotics are governed by Legge 7/1956 (pharmacist keeps a copy-prescription register and a carico/scarico register) and Legge 32/1988; these are state pharmacy duties. Wholesale of vet medicines needs a Dipartimento Prevenzione authorisation (bill text; belongs to the vet category). No San Marino rules were found on drug precursors, REACH or biocides. A bill on phytosanitary products (aligning with EU Reg. 1107/2009 and Dir. 2009/128, 18 articles, 7 annexes) was seen; whether it was enacted is unknown (see C3). No human-medicine wholesaler or importer regime found.

result.competitor: None found. Italian-language searches for San Marino dealer software and the register found only generic DMS listings on Capterra (e.g. CAMS DMS), with no San Marino register support. The register itself is a free state portal that auto-fills at the visto merci, so most of the core job is already done by the state.
result.duty: Confirmed in principle, specifics partly unverified. Parliament (Consiglio Grande e Generale) documents describe a digital register of vehicle-trade operators kept by ASE-CC. It covers operators with vehicle-trade ATECO codes. Vehicles are entered automatically at the visto merci, and operators must give per-vehicle data (make, model, chassis number, storage site, intended use) and record changes. A bank guarantee to the Chamber of Commerce is required from new operators and on changes of ownership. The 200,000 EUR figure appears only in a political news quote. The 48-hour deadline and the fine ladder (200 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 25,000 EUR) could not be checked: the official PDFs did not convert to text, and search excerpts did not show them. The register's implementing regulation was not found. This is San Marino law, ratified 2026. Related: DL 33/2026, a support package for the sector.
result.market: Exact count not found. A 2019 Osservatorio del Commercio report counts 1,066 active wholesale and retail trade firms including motor-vehicle repair (31 Dec 2018), which is a broad upper bound. Vehicle dealers proper are probably tens to low hundreds. The sector is in crisis after Italy's 2024 registration and VAT controls on San Marino vehicles.
result.reason: The duty is real, but the market is tiny and a software layer adds little. Official parliament documents describe a digital register of vehicle-trade operators kept by ASE-CC. Vehicles enter it automatically at the customs visto merci, and dealers add make, model, chassis number and storage site. No San Marino dealer tool or integration was found. But the state portal does most of the work, so a vendor would only add stock sync and storage-site alerts. The market is likely a few dozen to low hundreds of dealers in a sector in crisis, and the 200k guarantee shrinks it further. The implementing regulation and any API are still unknown. Pain comes from fines, not from workload.

The bill "Disposizioni sul noleggio di veicoli" (with DD 29 June 2026 n.85) is real, but I found no sign it has passed. The relazione covers written contracts, a register, 5-year retention, a cap of 70 vehicles and a portal run by the Ufficio Registro Automezzi. Existing rules already require operators to publish register data in real time on the state site autonoleggio.sm. So the state portal does the core job, and no vendor product turned up. The market is tiny: no operator count found, probably a handful of firms. Willingness to pay and distribution are weak. A niche add-on at best.

The duty exists but is thin. San Marino food premises need an ISS sanitary authorisation (Law 92/85 art. 10, as cited in the search result), and ISS veterinary inspection applies. The HACCP article reportedly excludes retail sales as defined by Law 65/2000. The ISS PDF in the claim was unreadable when fetched, and its metadata shows "Decreto 9 marzo 2005", not the 1993 decree the claim cites. I found no butcher count, penalty figures or recurring filing frequency. The market is a handful of firms in a country of about 34k people. No competing software was found, but the search was one query. The authorisation is largely one-off and the buyer pool is tiny, so this is a poor fit for a software product.

decisions.reason: New duty: dealer register with 48-hour entries under DD 85/2026; not covered by any known idea.
Rental operators are a new buyer group with a register and contract duty; the bill's status is for verifiers.
Small lodgings must withhold and remit tourist tax and record guests; a new buyer group and duty.
Recurring waste register and annual return under D.D. 44/2012; the small-firm exemptions need checking by verifiers.
Mandatory telematic visto merci for importers is a new duty. It is unverified and the rule may change.
Associations and foundations face register filings and a statute-adaptation deadline around September 2026; community bodies are in scope.
Small private clinics have authorisation and reporting duties; the duty falls on the clinics themselves.
Small licensed security firms have a licence and sworn-guard register duty; a new buyer group.
Same buyer (families employing a carer) and same payroll and permit duty as K02.
Domestic e-invoicing for the same operators is the duty in K03, K01 and K06.
Households and farms must hold UPAV water abstraction authorisations with renewals; a new duty.
Street vendors are sole traders with permit and renewal duties, a new buyer group; details are unverified.
Butchers and slaughterhouses are a different buyer group from K07 (organic and small food producers); it is related to K07, and verifiers should check the HACCP exclusion.
Farmers face a possible phytosanitary use register; whether the bill was enacted is unverified, so keep for checking.
